reason: The registered nonvanishing dichotomy gives only | ||Q||-1 | <= O(delta+epsilon)=O(e), not O(delta), so the asserted O(delta) norm control and the inference to two-sided (1+O(delta)) bounds are not licensed. This failure is concrete: for small epsilon>0 take A=C with ordinary product and involution, operator-space matrix norms ||X||_n=(1+epsilon/2)||X||_op, delta=0, and Q=1. This is an extended epsilon-C*-algebra (associativity is exact; the product, C*, unit, and Ruan bounds hold for small epsilon), Q is an exact projection with dim S_Q=1, but ||Q||=1+epsilon/2 is not 1+O(delta)=1. The weaker O(e) statement would support the final c_Q*e conclusion, but the node as written contains a false quantitative inference and must be corrected.
